concept.name: Consistency Patterns

spark.title: Consistency Patterns
spark.summary: Choose the right distributed consistency guarantee—from strict linearizability to causal, read-your-writes, and eventual convergence—based on user invariants and latency budgets.
spark.keyTakeaway: Strongest consistency (Linearizability) costs cross-AZ/region coordination latency; client-centric guarantees like Read-Your-Writes deliver intuitive UX at a fraction of the cost.
spark.byteSummary:
Choose the right distributed consistency guarantee—from strict linearizability to causal, read-your-writes, and eventual convergence—based on user invariants and latency budgets.

Picture a user updating their shipping address, hitting Refresh, and watching their old address reappear for two seconds.

Strongest consistency (Linearizability) costs cross-AZ/region coordination latency; client-centric guarantees like Read-Your-Writes deliver intuitive UX at a fraction of the cost.

concept.whyItMatters: Picture a user updating their shipping address, hitting Refresh, and watching their old address reappear for two seconds. Nothing crashed—the write committed to the [SQL](/domains/sql) primary, while the refresh landed on an asynchronous read replica lagging 400ms behind. Choosing the right consistency pattern lets you avoid paying global [Raft/Quorum](/concept/leader-election-patterns) latency on every read while still protecting user trust via session LSN routing.
whenToUse: Linearizability for distributed locks, leader leases, and unique username/inventory claims.
Read-Your-Writes & Monotonic Reads for user profiles, comments, and settings.
Causal Consistency for threaded discussions and collaborative state.
whenNotToUse: Paying cross-region consensus latency for analytics counters or view counts where eventual consistency suffices.
keyPoints: Linearizability provides a single global real-time order: once a write completes, every subsequent read anywhere sees it or a newer value.
Causal Consistency preserves happens-before relationships (e.g., question before answer) without blocking on unrelated concurrent writes.
Read-Your-Writes ensures a user always sees their own recent mutations—achievable via sticky replica routing, session LSN tokens, or reading from primary for N seconds after a write.
Monotonic Reads guarantees time never appears to move backward across consecutive reads (pinning a user to a replica or minimum LSN).

examples.title: Session-Token Read-Your-Writes Routing
examples.scenario: A user updates their display name (committed at primary WAL `LSN = 9042`) and immediately reloads `/profile`, which hits a read replica currently at `LSN = 9038`.
examples.outcome: The client sends `X-Min-LSN: 9042` in its session cookie; the router either waits briefly for the replica to catch up to `9042` or falls back to the primary, preventing the 'disappearing edit' bug.

tradeOffs.con: Requires quorum round-trips and fails writes during minority partitions

tradeOffs.pro: Fast replica reads most of the time

failureModes.name: Replication Lag Breaking Read-Your-Writes
failureModes.description: Write hits primary, immediate refresh hits lagging replica and returns old state.
failureModes.mitigation: Route recent writers to primary for a short window or enforce `min_lsn` on replicas.

failureModes.name: Replica Hopping Breaking Monotonic Reads
failureModes.description: Request 1 hits Replica A (LSN 100); Request 2 hits lagging Replica B (LSN 92), so data disappears.
failureModes.mitigation: Pin user session to one replica or pass `last_seen_lsn`.

commonMistakes: Confusing ACID Consistency (database constraint validity) with CAP/Distributed Consistency (linearizability across replicas).
Assuming Eventual Consistency means no coordination is needed—applications still need conflict resolution (LWW, CRDTs) and idempotency.

sections.content:
## Consistency spectrum & real-world mechanisms

| Pattern | Scope | Guarantees | Typical Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Linearizable | Global (data-centric) | Real-time single-copy illusion | Raft / Paxos quorum reads (`ReadIndex`) |
| Sequential | Global | Same order for all nodes, not real-time | Single-sequencer log |
| Causal | Partial order | Preserves cause-before-effect | Vector clocks / Hybrid Logical Clocks |
| Read-Your-Writes | Per-client session | User always sees own writes | Primary-pin window or `min_lsn` cookie |
| Monotonic Reads | Per-client session | Reads never go backward in time | Sticky replica or `last_seen_lsn` |
| Eventual | Global convergence | Converges when writes cease | Async replication + LWW / CRDT |

pillars.label: All Patterns
pillars.summary: Consistency patterns determine whether reads can use fast lagging replicas or must coordinate with the primary/quorum.

pillars.label: Linearizable
pillars.summary: Every read routes to the quorum leader (or ReadIndex) so stale replicas are never observed.

pillars.label: Read-Your-Writes
pillars.summary: Router compares replica LSN against the client's session min_lsn and falls back to primary only if the replica lags behind that user's write.

normal.heading: Step 1: Mutation Commits on Primary (LSN 9042)
normal.desc: User updates profile on Primary; server returns cookie `min_lsn=9042`.

normal.heading: Step 2: Replica Reaches LSN 9042
normal.desc: Replica replays WAL to 9042. Router serves the reload directly from the fast replica.

normal.heading: Step 3: Steady-State Replica Reads
normal.desc: Subsequent reads hit replicas whenever replica_lsn >= min_lsn.

fault.heading: Step 3 (LAG!): Replica Stuck at LSN 9038
fault.desc: Replica lags at 9038 < 9042. Router detects `replica_lsn < min_lsn` and routes this single read to Primary.

failureMiniDiagrams.topLabel: WRITE TO PRIMARY → READ STALE REPLICA

checklist: Classify each endpoint: does it require Linearizability (inventory/locks), Read-Your-Writes (user settings), or Eventual (counters)?
Pass session LSN or write-timestamp tokens so users never see their own edits disappear.
Monitor replication lag p99 and alert before fallback traffic overwhelms the primary.

putItTogether.title: Put Consistency Patterns together
putItTogether.summary: Reserve linearizable quorum reads for locks and financial balances, enforce Read-Your-Writes via session LSN cookies for user profiles, and let analytics counters converge eventually.
steps: Use Raft/quorum linearizability for locks, balances, and unique constraints.
Propagate `min_lsn` in user sessions to enforce Read-Your-Writes and Monotonic Reads over read replicas.
Use Causal / CRDT models for multi-region collaboration without cross-ocean locking.
putItTogether.outcome: Low-latency local reads for 99% of traffic with strict safety where invariants require it.

tipsAndTricks: Linearizability is about real-time global order; Causal consistency only orders causally related events.
Read-Your-Writes is a per-client guarantee—other users may still see eventual convergence a few milliseconds later.

questions.prompt: A user edits their bio and refreshes the page, only to see the old bio for 2 seconds because the read hit a lagging replica. Which consistency guarantee was violated?

options.explanation: Read-Your-Writes ensures a client always observes its own completed writes.
The write was durable on the primary; the replica simply lagged.
Atomicity governs all-or-nothing commit, not cross-replica visibility.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
